title: Adjectives in depth: this, that, own, whole
title_target: Nu har du ett eget rum
goal: Put adjectives and nouns together correctly after *den här*, *den där*, possessives, *egen*, *liten* and *hela / halva* — the spots where even advanced learners slip.
bekal: you can point things out: *den här lilla lampan*, *det där gamla bordet*, *de här små kopparna*
you can combine a possessive and an adjective: *min nya cykel*, *Jonas nya cykel*
you can use *egen / eget / egna*, *liten / litet / lilla / små* and *hela / halva*
wave: Go back to Unit 7: say the reflexive verbs *sätta sig, lägga sig, känna sig, skynda sig, gifta sig, vänja sig vid* with every person (*jag sätter mig, du sätter dig…*), then make one past-tense sentence with each.

dialogs.title: Dialogue — På loppis
dialogs.intro: A sunny Saturday at the flea market on Hornstull's riverside. Dian is hunting for things for her new room, and Jonas is still looking for a bike to replace the stolen one.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Titta, Jonas! Den där lilla lampan passar perfekt i mitt rum.
lines.id: Look, Jonas! That little lamp is perfect for my room.
lines.literal: look, Jonas! that there little lamp-the fits perfect in my room.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Nu har du ett eget rum. Då behöver du egna saker!
lines.id: Now you've got your own room. So you need your own things!
lines.literal: now have you an own room. then need you own things!

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Precis. I korridoren delade jag allt, till och med kylskåpet.
lines.id: Exactly. In the corridor I shared everything, even the fridge.
lines.literal: exactly. in corridor-the shared I everything, to and with fridge-the.

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Lampan är från sextiotalet. Ni får den för halva priset: hundra kronor.
lines.id: The lamp's from the sixties. You can have it for half price: a hundred kronor.
lines.literal: lamp-the is from sixties-the. you get it for half price-the: hundred crowns.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.id: A hundred kronor? I'll take it!

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Och den där blå cykeln, vad kostar den?
lines.id: And that blue bike, how much is it?
lines.literal: and that there blue bike-the, what costs it?

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Sexhundra. Det är min dotters gamla, men hon har en egen bil nu.
lines.id: Six hundred. It's my daughter's old one, but she has her own car now.
lines.literal: six-hundred. it is my daughter's old, but she has an own car now.

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Bromsarna ser nya ut. Får jag prova den?
lines.id: The brakes look new. Can I try it?
lines.literal: brakes-the look new out. may I try it?

lines.speaker: Jonas:
lines.text: Perfekt! Min nya cykel! Du får tillbaka din ikväll, Dian.
lines.id: Perfect! My new bike! You'll get yours back tonight, Dian.
lines.literal: perfect! my new bike! you get back yours tonight, Dian.

lines.speaker: Dian:
lines.text: Bra, för jag har saknat den hela veckan.
lines.id: Good, because I've missed it all week.
lines.literal: good, for I have missed it whole week-the.

lines.speaker: Säljaren:
lines.text: Vill ni ha de här små kopparna också? Ni får alla sex för femtio.
lines.id: Would you like these little cups too? You can have all six for fifty.
lines.literal: want you have these here small cups-the too? you get all six for fifty.

lines.text: De är så söta! Och det lilla gula bordet då?

lines.text: Kom, vi går innan hela Södermalm har köpt allt.

lines.literal: come, we go before whole Södermalm has bought everything.

lines.text: En lampa, sex koppar och Jonas nya cykel. Bra dag!
lines.id: A lamp, six cups and Jonas's new bike. Good day!

notes: **Den där lilla lampan** — after *den här* / *den där* (this / that), Swedish marks the noun as definite **twice**: the adjective takes *-a* and the noun keeps its end article. Word for word, "that there little the-lamp". So: *den här lamp**an***, *det där gamla bord**et***, *de här små kopp**arna***. Leaving off the ending (*den här lampa*) is the single most common mistake with this pattern.

**Ett eget rum, egna saker** — *egen* (own) has three forms: *en egen bil*, *ett eget rum*, *egna saker*. Unlike other adjectives, it keeps that form **after a possessive**: *min egen bil*, *mitt **eget** rum*. You will hear *mitt egna rum* in casual speech, but in writing stick with *eget*. Note also that Swedish says *ett eget rum* where English says "my own room" — the possessive is often left out.

**Lilla, små** — *liten* is the most irregular adjective in the language: *en liten lampa*, *ett litet bord*, *den lilla lampan*, and in the plural *små* — both *små koppar* and *de små kopparna*. In the dialogue you hear all of them: *den där lilla lampan*, *de här små kopparna*, *det lilla gula bordet*.

**Min dotters gamla**, **Jonas nya cykel** — after a possessive (*min*, *din*, *Jonas*, *min dotters*), the adjective takes *-a*, but the noun stays **without** its ending: *min **nya cykel***, never *min nya cykeln*. The possessive already makes it definite. *Min dotters* is a genitive: *dotter* + *-s*.

**Halva priset, hela veckan, hela Södermalm** — *hela* (whole) and *halva* (half) go straight in front of a definite noun, with no *den*: *hela dag**en***, *halva tid**en***. With a name there is no ending to add: *hela Sverige*, *hela Södermalm*. Remember the pronunciation: **HEH-lah**, **HAHL-vah**.

**Loppis** (short for *loppmarknad*, "flea market") is a Swedish passion — on summer weekends every town square, school yard and garage seems to have one. People say *gå på loppis* with no article, just as they say *gå på bio*. **Den tar jag!** puts the object first for emphasis: "That one I'll take!" — V2 still holds, so *tar* comes second.

grammars.title: When does the adjective take -a?
body: The adjective takes its *-a* form every time the noun phrase is definite. What changes is whether the **noun** keeps its own end article.
after: So there are just two patterns to learn. **Pointing words** (*den, den här, den där*) → double definite: adjective *-a* **and** noun ending. **Owner words** (possessives and genitives) → adjective *-a*, bare noun.
*Blå* is the one common color that does not add *-a*: *den där blå cykeln*, *min blå tröja*. In speech you will also hear *blåa*, which is fine but informal.

grammars.title: Four adjectives with a will of their own
body: Most adjectives follow the *stor / stort / stora* pattern you know. These four do not — and they are among the most frequent words in Swedish.

head: Adjective
en-word
ett-word
definite / after possessive
plural
rows: den lilla lampan · min lilla lampa
min egen bil · mitt eget rum
den gamla stolen · min gamla stol

after: Note the double letters disappearing: *gammal* → *gamla*, and *annan* → *andra*. *Liten* changes completely in the plural — think of English "little" vs "small".
*Hela* and *halva* never change: *hela dagen*, *hela året*, *hela veckan*; *halva priset*, *halva tiden*.

sections.title: Ten phrases to say until they sound right

blocks.text: These patterns are learned by the ear, not by the rule. Read the left column aloud three times, cover it, and rebuild each phrase from the English.

blocks.title: Four mistakes to avoid
items: *den här lampa* → **den här lampan** (the noun keeps its ending)
*min nya cykeln* → **min nya cykel** (no ending after a possessive)
*en lilla lampa* → **en liten lampa** (*lilla* only in the definite)

blocks.text: Haggling is allowed at a *loppis*, but gently. A good opening is a question, not an offer: *Kan du tänka dig hundra?* ("Would you consider a hundred?"). And if you find something great for almost nothing, Swedes will say you made *ett fynd* — the word for a lucky find, and a word every second-hand shopper loves.

blocks.title: Spiral review — back to Unit 8
items: Explain your buys with a reason: *Jag köpte den lilla lampan eftersom den var billig.* *Jonas köpte en cykel, därför får jag tillbaka min.*
Then a purpose: *Jag gick på loppis för att hitta egna saker till mitt rum.*

exercises.prompt: Fill in the correct form of the adjective in brackets.

Det där ____ bordet är redan sålt. (gammal)
Vi har våra ____ saker i köket. (egen)

exercises.prompt: Write the noun in brackets in the right form: with or without its ending.
